- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then gradually decline — suggesting a lag in recognizing mean reversion.
- After a spike in price (e.g., 74+), model often overreacts with a prolonged high forecast, failing to adjust downward quickly.
- Model underestimates the true mean of recent 30-day history, particularly in the latter half of the forecast.
- Forecasts show a strong bias toward higher values in the first 5–10 days, then drift downward — possibly due to ignoring recent downward momentum.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after high peaks; true outcomes often show a more abrupt drop than forecasted.
- When history includes a recent low (e.g., 68–70), model tends to ignore it and overreacts to subsequent small increases.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts are too optimistic when recent prices are trending up, but too pessimistic when trending down.
